canonical_question: Does the boundary obstacle stress (σ_b0) act uniformly across all precipitates, or does its effectiveness vary with precipitate size and spacing?

question_variants.question: Does the boundary obstacle stress (σ_b0) act uniformly across all precipitates, or does its effectiveness vary with precipitate size and spacing?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text states that precipitates formed along grain boundaries exert a boundary obstacle stress σ_b0. It does not explicitly clarify if this stress acts uniformly across all precipitates or if its effectiveness varies with precipitate size and spacing, although such variation is implied in general materials science principles not stated in the text.

answers.answer: The precipitates are predominantly formed along the grain boundaries and would exert a boundary obstacle stress σ_b0. The text does not explicitly state whether this stress acts uniformly or varies with precipitate size and spacing.
answers.mechanism: Precipitates act as barriers via boundary obstacle stress
answers.boundary_limitation: No explicit detail on uniformity or variation with size/spacing of σ_b0
evidence_spans: The observed jog configurations are indicative of a dislocation climb process, and thus the stress-assisted dislocation climb controlled by lattice diffusion may be the operative creep mechanism of the present high-entropy alloy in LSR.
Contrary to LSR, creep deformation in HSR exhibits abnormally high stress exponents of 8.9–14 and an average activation energy of 380 kJ mol −1 .
As shown in Figure 6 , obvious dynamic recrystallization occurred in the present CoCrFeNiMn alloy in HSR.
